key_insight: Diffusion generation expands ABX₃ perovskite chemistry and structural diversity, but does not establish enrichment in candidates near the 1.4 eV bandgap target.
engineering_relevance: The workflow could broaden photovoltaic absorber screening, provided generated candidates pass topology, relaxation and electronic-property checks.
method: Generate candidate ABX₃ crystals with a pretrained diffusion model.
Filter for three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskite connectivity.
Evaluate ALIGNN-predicted bandgaps and perform first-principles checks on six structures.
evidence_signal: The generated target-window fraction was 8.2% versus 7.3% for the Materials Project reference; ALIGNN performed well on a formula-grouped random split but failed to beat a constant baseline on a severe B-site-disjoint test.
watch_item: Different MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent a target-enrichment claim, while relaxation can change topology and calculated gaps can differ appreciably from predictions.
paper_title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
